turns.user: We're taking a truck of goods up towards the Afghan border next month and a friend said officials can stop and search carts and packages for arms at searching posts along the border. Which section of the Arms Act, 1878 actually allows that?

gold.answer: Section 11 of the Arms Act, 1878 allows the Federal Government to set up searching-posts along the boundary-line between Pakistan and foreign territory, where vessels, carts, baggage-animals and packages in transit may be stopped and searched for arms, ammunition and military stores.

evidence.quote: at any places along the boundary-line between [Pakistan] and foreign territory
searching-posts at which all vessels, carts and baggage-animals, and all boxes, bales and packages in transit, may be stopped and searched for arms, ammunition and military stores

turns.user: My uncle mortgaged his land and I stood surety for the loan. Can I sue for redemption of the mortgaged property myself, or is that only for the mortgagor? Which section of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 covers this?

gold.answer: Yes. Under section 91 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, besides the mortgagor, any surety for the payment of the mortgage-debt may redeem or institute a suit for redemption of the mortgaged property.

evidence.quote: Besides the mortgagor, any of the following persons may redeem, or institute a suit for redemption of, the mortgaged property
any surety for the payment of the mortgage

turns.user: In Abu Bakar v. First Women Bank Ltd. (I.A. No. 74 of 2014), decided by the Sindh High Court on 5.10.2018, the appellant claimed some of the bank's documents were forged. Why wasn't that enough to get him leave to defend?

gold.answer: Because the appellant admitted that the mortgage had been created, the bald allegation that some of the other documents were forged was not per se a substantial question of fact requiring evidence under Section 10 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001.

evidence.quote: the bald allegation that some of the other documents were forged, is not per se a "substantial question of fact in respect of which evidence needs to be recorded" within the meaning of Section 10 of the Financial Institutions (Recovery of Finances) Ordinance, 2001
In the circumstances where the creation of the mortgage is admitted

gold.answer: The Court said the decree holder may approach the Nazir of the Court to seek a refund of the money she deposited on 9.1.2017.

turns.user: Last year Abbu gave me his house as a gift, of his own free will and without taking any money, and I accepted it. He's still alive, thank God.
My bhabi keeps making comments about it at family dinners.
The house is quite old and needs a lot of repair work.
I've kept the file with all the papers at my office.
So going back to what I said at the start, which section of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines that kind of transfer?

gold.answer: Section 122 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defines a gift: a voluntary transfer of existing property without consideration, accepted by the donee.

evidence.quote: the transfer of certain existing moveable or immoveable property made voluntarily and without consideration, by one person, called the donor, to another, called the donee, and accepted by or on behalf of the donee

turns.user: In 2023 I signed a continuing guarantee with a wholesaler in Sukkur for whatever my brother buys from him on credit.
My brother runs a small kiryana store near the bus stand.
I teach maths at a government school, so I don't have much time for all this.
I'm seeing a lawyer friend on Monday.
I want to send the wholesaler a notice now. Thinking back to my first message, which section of the Contract Act, 1872 lets me revoke it?

gold.answer: Section 130 of the Contract Act, 1872: a continuing guarantee may be revoked by the surety at any time, as to future transactions, by notice to the creditor.

evidence.quote: A continuing guarantee may at any time be revoked by the surety, as to future transactions, by notice to the creditor.
